tecidos/fundamentos-dos-tecidos/tissue-b.descricaoOriginal: Tissues are groups of cells organized for specific functions. The four tissue types, epithelial, connective, muscle and nervous, differ in composition and appearance, reflecting their various functions. Epithelial, muscle and nervous tissues are composed of closely packed cells with little extracellular material. Connective tissues are unique in their abundant extracellular components along with various cells types. Left: 1000x, 400x; Right: 600x, 600x

base.alt: Fotomicrografia de Basic tissues: Epithelial and connective — Tecidos › Fundamentos dos Tecidos › Fundamentos dos tecidos 1.

overlays.explicacaoOriginal: Epithelial tissues consist of closely-spaced cells, arranged in single or multiple layers, that both line or cover all body surfaces as well as form glands. Single-layer epithelia often have surface specializations, like cilia seen here. Individual cells are bound together by junctions that isolate the surface space from the intercellular space, thus providing integrity to the epithelial layer. All epithelia rest on a basement membrane.

overlays.explicacaoOriginal: Connective tissues possess cells and an abundant extracellular matrix. The matrix, imparting unique functions to this tissue, is composed of ground substance (with the consistency of a liquid, a gel or a flexible rubber) and fibers (providing a framework and strength). Major connective tissue types include blood, connective tissue proper, cartilage and bone.

tecidos/fundamentos-dos-tecidos/tissue-b.descricaoOriginal: The four tissues of the body include epithelium, connective tissue, muscle and nervous. Muscle and nervous tissue are illustrated in this image. Left: 400x, 600x; Right: 400x, 400x

overlays.explicacaoOriginal: Muscle tissue is composed of abundant cells and minimal extracellular matrix. Muscle cells are elongate in shape and usually clustered into bundles with a similar orientation, so that they produce coordinated contraction. Muscle tissue is broadly classified as either non-striated (smooth muscle) or striated (skeletal and cardiac muscle). Striations, shown in this section of skeletal muscle, appear as distinct cross-bands in the cells.

overlays.explicacaoOriginal: Nervous tissue, with abundant cells and minimal extracellular matrix, is composed of nerve cells (neurons) and their supporting cells. Neurons are specialized to conduct electrical impulses, convey sensory stimuli from the environment, and produce appropriate motor responses. Additionally, nervous tissue provides integration and storage of information.

They differ in composition, appearance and location, reflecting their various functions. The four types of tissues are epithelial, connective, muscle and nervous, each of which is present in this section of the stomach wall. 100x

overlays.explicacaoOriginal: Epithelial cells can be arranged in single or multiple layers, forming membranes that line or cover all body surfaces. For example, a multilayered epithelium forms the outer layer of the skin as well as the inner surface of the oral cavity and esophagus. Single-layered epithelia line most internal surfaces, such as blood vessels and body cavities.

midia.alt: Camada de marcação destacando Epitélio de revestimento em Basic tissues in organs.

overlays.explicacaoOriginal: Glands consist of epithelial cells modified to secrete a product. Exocrine glands (shown here) are attached to a lining epithelium and secrete onto its surface. Endocrine glands lose their attachment with an epithelium and secrete into the blood stream. Glands may be microscopic like these gastric glands or large, macroscopic glands such as salivary glands.

midia.alt: Camada de marcação destacando Epitélio glandular em Basic tissues in organs.

overlays.explicacaoOriginal: Connective tissue proper is one of the major categories of connective tissues; other categories include cartilage, bone and blood. All connective tissues are characterized by an abundant extracellular matrix surrounding cells, consisting of fibers, ground substance and tissue fluid. Connective tissue proper, also called fibrous connective tissue, is widely distributed throughout organs and is subdivided into two major categories, loose connective tissue and dense connective tissue. These designations are based on the arrangement and size of the collagen fibers and the number and types of cells present.

overlays.explicacaoOriginal: Nervous tissue is composed of nerve cells (neurons) and their supporting cells. Most nervous tissue is concentrated in the brain and spinal cord, with nerves extending into the periphery. The nervous tissue indicated here regulates the contraction of smooth muscle in the wall of the stomach.

tecidos/fundamentos-dos-tecidos/tissue-b.descricaoOriginal: Tissues can also form structures that are not usually thought of as organs. However, because they are formed by two or more tissues, they are truly organs. Examples shown here are bone, skin and blood vessels. 100x, 100x, 400x

overlays.explicacaoOriginal: Bone is an organ because it is composed of several types of connective tissue (the tissue bone, bone marrow, and a connective tissue proper covering), blood vessels (composed of epithelium and muscle), and nerves.

overlays.explicacaoOriginal: Skin is composed of epithelial tissues, forming a surface epidermis and deeper glands along with a connective tissue layer that forms the dermis. Blood vessels and nerves are also present.

overlays.explicacaoOriginal: Two of these organs have a free surface and, therefore, are lined by an epithelium. The free surface of the skin is the exterior surface of the body and the free surface of the artery is the lumen through which blood flows.

overlays.explicacaoOriginal: Bone, another type of connective tissue, has a firm, calcified matrix that gives bone its rigidity. Bone cells are present within the matrix and on the bone surface.

overlays.explicacaoOriginal: The spaces within bone are filled with a special type of connective tissue called bone marrow.

overlays.explicacaoOriginal: Muscle is a frequent component of organs and forms a majority of the arterial wall. Muscle also forms an important component in the walls of other hollow organs, as seen in the previous image of the stomach. Smooth muscle is also present in the skin, where it is attached to hair follicles. Muscle is absent in bone, except in the walls of vessels supplying the bones.
